items.title: Putative duplication glyph in the rongorongo script
items.note: Argues from the genealogy section of the Small Santiago Tablet and wider syntax that the 'split circles' glyph marks reduplication.

items.title: Allographs, graphic variants and iconic formulae in the kohau rongorongo script of Rapa Nui (Easter Island)
items.note: Defines allograph, graphic variant and iconic formula for rongorongo and proposes an inverse substitution method for testing sign equivalences.

items.title: ERC project INSCRIBE: Invention of Scripts and their Beginnings (2018–2024)
items.note: Six-year grant on the independent invention of writing that funded 3D modelling and radiocarbon dating of the Rome rongorongo tablets.

items.title: 3D modelling of the Mamari tablet from the rongorongo corpus: acquisition, processing issues, and outcomes
items.who: L. Lastilla, R. Ravanelli, M. Valério and S. Ferrara
items.note: First high-resolution 3D digitization of Tablet C (Mamari) in Rome, as a basis for palaeographic study independent of older editions.

items.title: rongopy: ideas for the decipherment of Easter Island's rongorongo writing
items.note: Open Python code and a reduced transliteration of the corpus for statistical and algorithmic decipherment experiments, later tested by other researchers.

items.title: Rongorongo: Inscribed Objects from Rapa Nui
items.note: Corpus edition with photographs and drawings of all known rongorongo inscribed objects.

items.title: Modelling the Rongorongo tablets: A new transcription of the Échancrée tablet and the foundation for decipherment attempts
items.who: L. Lastilla, R. Ravanelli, M. Valério and S. Ferrara
items.note: Used 3D models to produce a revised transcription of Tablet D, correcting readings in earlier editions.

items.title: Hatching in the Hieroglyphic Script and Iconography of Easter Island (Rapa Nui): Comparison with Maya and Nahuatl Scripts
items.note: Compares the use of hatching in rongorongo signs and Rapa Nui iconography with Mesoamerican scripts to infer its graphic function.

items.title: The rongorongo tablet from Berlin and the time-depth of Easter Island's writing system
items.who: R. M. Wieczorek, K. E. Frankiewicz, A. A. Oskolski and P. Horley
items.venue: Journal of Island and Coastal Archaeology
items.note: Identified the Berlin Tablet's wood as locally grown Thespesia populnea, not driftwood, and radiocarbon-dated it to the early nineteenth century.

items.title: A wooden hand from Easter Island (Rapa Nui), part I
items.who: R. M. Schoch and T. S. Melka
items.note: Describes the 'Kell Hand', a carved hand collected during the 1868 HMS Topaze visit that bears a short rongorongo inscription.

items.title: The script of Rapa Nui (Easter Island) is logosyllabic, the language is East Polynesian: evidence from cross-readings
items.note: Argues from cross-readings between parallel passages that the script is logosyllabic and records an East Polynesian language.

items.title: The invention of writing on Rapa Nui (Easter Island). New radiocarbon dates on the Rongorongo script
items.note: Dated four Rome tablets; three are late, but Tablet D's non-native wood gave a fifteenth-century felling date, read by the authors as suggesting pre-contact writing.

items.title: Was rongorongo an independent invention of writing?
items.note: Replied that a felling date is only a terminus post quem for carving and that rongorongo has not been shown to encode language.

items.title: The "Topaze stick fragment": a newly discovered rongorongo-inscribed artifact collected during the Rapa Nui (Easter Island) visit of HMS Topaze in 1868
items.who: T. S. Melka and R. M. Schoch
items.note: Documents and analyses a second short inscription on a wooden object from the 1868 Topaze visit, previously unknown to the literature.

items.title: The Rongorongo 'Lunar Calendar' of Rapa Nui (Easter Island) and the Type of Script
items.venue: Writing from Invention to Decipherment (Oxford University Press)
items.note: Re-examines Guy's Mamari calendar passage and what it implies about the typology of the script.

items.title: A statistical reassessment of rongorongo texts I, Gv, and T: implications for genre and content
items.note: Collocation analysis suggests the Santiago Staff contains personal names and that Gv parallels the Atua-Mata-Riri creation chant, reopening Fischer's procreation reading for that text.

items.title: A Computational Evaluation of Syllabic Hypotheses for Rongorongo: Evidence from N-gram Analysis
items.note: Genetic-algorithm tests against Rapa Nui n-gram statistics find no simple one-sign-one-syllable signal in the CEIPP transliteration, with ambiguous results for rongopy's.

items.title: A rongorongo-inscribed artifact collected by Pascal Boucher, a crewmember of the whaling ship Margaret Rait during her call to Easter Island (Rapa Nui) in December 1843
items.who: T. S. Melka and R. M. Schoch
items.note: Publishes a privately held inscribed pendant reportedly collected in 1843, which would place it before the missionary period if the provenance holds.

items.title: Computational analysis reveals historical trajectory of East Polynesian lunar calendars
items.who: M. Valério, F. Tamburini, M. Corazza et al.
items.note: Phylogenetic analysis of 48 'nights of the moon' lists groups Rapa Nui with Mangareva and the Marquesas, relevant to reading calendrical passages on the tablets.
